text: When Laura was called to the telephone, she met her brother Laurie in the hall, and, giving him a small quick squeeze, she cried, Oh, I do love parties. <break time="0.8s" /> On the telephone she invited Kitty Maitland to lunch, while her mothers voice floated down the stairs, telling Laura that Kitty must wear the sweet hat she had worn last Sunday. <break time="0.8s" /> The house was alive with quick steps and running voices, and little spots of sunlight played on the inkpot and the silver photograph frame, as if they too were enjoying the day. <break time="0.8s" /> A man from the florist arrived with a wide tray full of pink canna lilies, so many that Laura cried out in surprise, and her mother confessed that she had ordered them herself. <break time="0.8s" /> I saw them in a shop window yesterday, said Missus Sheridan, and I suddenly thought that for once in my life I would have enough canna lilies. <break time="0.8s" /> In the drawing room Jose tested the piano by singing a sad song about a weary life, and then she smiled a brilliant, unsympathetic smile, sure that she was in good voice. <break time="0.8s" /> In the kitchen there were fifteen different kinds of sandwiches, and the cook, who had made every one of them, smiled with pride when Jose praised her work. <break time="0.8s" /> When the man from Godbers brought cream puffs, the cook let each girl have one, and soon they were licking whipped cream from their fingers.
